batch-scorer.label: Bulk Scorer
batch-scorer.one_liner: N items in, a typed judgment on each, ranked or filtered out.
batch-scorer.shape: source -> normalise -> fan-out typed calls -> store -> browse
batch-scorer.why_jev: Cost and latency scale linearly with N. At 3,000+ items an LLM is unaffordable; a typed call at ~$0.042/M input is not.

feed-filter.label: Live Feed Filter
feed-filter.one_liner: Classify DOM nodes as they appear and hide, tag or recolour them.
feed-filter.shape: MutationObserver -> extract node text -> typed call -> mutate DOM
feed-filter.why_jev: Must decide in the gap before the user scrolls past. ~100ms works, 2s does not.
exemplars: Detecting slop in the X timeline

browser-agent.label: Browser / Computer Agent
browser-agent.one_liner: Indexed DOM snapshot in, one typed action out, loop until done.
browser-agent.shape: snapshot -> index elements -> single typed call -> execute -> repeat
browser-agent.why_jev: Replaces a screenshot+reasoning round-trip per step. Measured 1,092 -> 101 protocol calls.

router-gate.label: Router / Gate
router-gate.one_liner: Middleware that picks a branch, or blocks a risky one, before work happens.
router-gate.shape: intercept -> typed call -> dispatch | block | escalate
router-gate.why_jev: It sits on the hot path of every request, so it must be near-free and never the bottleneck.

control-loop.label: Real-time Control Loop
control-loop.one_liner: Game or physical state in, next move out, at frame rate.
control-loop.shape: sense state -> serialise -> typed move choice -> actuate -> repeat
control-loop.why_jev: A frame budget is ~16ms-100ms. Only a typed decision fits.

semantic-search.label: Semantic Search & Rank
semantic-search.one_liner: Score every candidate against what the user meant, then order them.
semantic-search.shape: candidates -> typed relevance score each -> sort -> present
semantic-search.why_jev: Scoring every candidate individually is only affordable when each score is ~free.

adaptive-ui.label: Adaptive Interface
adaptive-ui.one_liner: A typed decision chooses what the UI shows or asks next.
adaptive-ui.shape: user input -> typed call -> pick next component/field/format -> render
adaptive-ui.why_jev: It runs between keystrokes, so the decision has to beat the user's typing.

voice-intent.label: Voice & Intent Dispatch
voice-intent.one_liner: Speech in, a typed intent out, a function call executed.
voice-intent.shape: mic -> VAD -> STT -> typed intent + slots -> dispatch -> TTS
voice-intent.why_jev: Voice feels broken past ~300ms round-trip; the decision stage must cost ~100ms.
exemplars: Real-time voice control for a browser
An assistant without a wake word

ci-gate.label: Pipeline Quality Gate
ci-gate.one_liner: An artifact meets N typed checks and passes or fails with a reason.
ci-gate.shape: diff/doc -> N parallel typed checks -> aggregate -> pass | fail
ci-gate.why_jev: All N checks ride in one call, so adding a check is nearly free.
exemplars: Fourteen checks for every pull request

context-manager.label: Agent Context Manager
context-manager.one_liner: Score what an agent is carrying and drop what is not earning its place.
context-manager.shape: context items -> relevance score each -> prune -> resume
context-manager.why_jev: Pruning must cost far less than the tokens it saves, or it is pointless.

blueprints.name: Fit Finder for hard-to-fit bodies
blueprints.jtbd: When I am outside the sizes shops design for, I want to know which specific garment will actually fit me, so I stop ordering three sizes and returning two.
blueprints.who: Shoppers at the edges of the size curve. Plus-size, tall, petite, asymmetric, post-surgery.
blueprints.why_now: Every brand publishes a different size chart and none of them agree. That is a normalisation problem, and normalisation at catalogue scale is exactly what a cheap typed judgment is for.
blueprints.jev_role: Normalises each garment against a body profile: cut, stretch, rise, shoulder slope, and a fit verdict with a confidence number. One typed call per garment.
blueprints.not_jev: Catalogue scraping, size-chart OCR, the try-on render, and the shop front are all ordinary engineering. Jev is maybe 10% of the code.

phases.name: Corpus
phases.detail: Scrape 3-5 brands. Look for an embedded JSON blob before you render anything. Store garment, size chart, fabric, and the product image.

phases.name: Normalise
phases.detail: Size charts are images and inconsistent tables. OCR them into one schema: chest, waist, hip, inseam, stretch percentage.

phases.name: Judge
phases.detail: One typed call per garment against the body profile. Choice for fit verdict, Score for confidence in each dimension, Noul for the dealbreakers.

phases.name: Rank
phases.detail: Retrieve wide with filters, then order the shortlist by the typed score. Never score the whole catalogue live.

phases.name: Try on
phases.detail: Render the top few garments on the body. Strictly off the critical path - precompute or stream it.

phases.name: Ask out loud
phases.detail: Voice input for the profile. Speaking measurements beats typing them on a phone.

hard_parts: Size charts are pictures, not data. OCR quality decides the whole product.
Try-on rendering is 2-30s. Put it behind the ranked list, never in front of it.
A wrong fit verdict costs a return, so gate on confidence and say 'unsure' out loud.
blueprints.moat: The normalised size-chart corpus. The model is rentable; the corpus is not.

blueprints.name: Curriculum content factory for every class
blueprints.jtbd: When I teach or study a syllabus, I want every section rendered in several study modes with a grounded tutor, so a student can revise the way that suits them without me authoring it five times.
blueprints.who: Ed-tech builders, teachers, and anyone turning a public syllabus into a study product.
blueprints.why_now: The gallery has exactly ONE education project out of 359. The category is empty while the capability is ready.
blueprints.jev_role: Every quality gate and routing decision. Is this section complete, is this question answerable from the source, which difficulty tier, is this glossary term depictable, does this answer stray off-syllabus.
blueprints.not_jev: PDF to markdown, the authoring model, image generation, the reader UI, and the tutor chat are the bulk of the build.

phases.name: Source
phases.detail: Official chapter PDFs to clean markdown with a real text layer. OCR only where you must.

phases.name: Author
phases.detail: A strong model reproduces the canonical text faithfully. This is the one place to spend real tokens.

phases.name: Gate
phases.detail: Typed checks per section: coverage, factual traceability, equation balance. All checks ride in ONE call.

phases.name: Derive modes
phases.detail: Cards, flashcards, graded questions and a glossary, all derived from the canonical text, never re-authored.

phases.name: Illustrate
phases.detail: Typed call decides which terms are depictable at all, then generate only those. Skip the rest.

phases.name: Ground the tutor
phases.detail: The chatbot answers only from the active section. A typed call detects off-topic and redirects.

evidence: Fourteen checks for every pull request
hard_parts: Faithfulness beats fluency. A confident wrong equation is worse than no content.
Image generation is the pole. Precompute it off the critical path or a chapter takes twenty minutes instead of three.
Rate limits, not cost, cap throughput at about 20 typed calls a second.
blueprints.moat: The derived, quality-gated corpus per chapter. Re-deriving is cheap; the gates are the asset.

blueprints.name: Back-of-label scanner and scorer
blueprints.jtbd: When I pick up a packaged food, I want to know in one second whether it clears my household rules, so I can decide in the aisle.
blueprints.who: Parents, people with allergies, anyone on a medical diet.
blueprints.why_now: One shipped project scored 3,000 snacks on multiple criteria in 28 seconds for $0.11. The economics are already proven in public.
blueprints.jev_role: Scores the parsed ingredient list against each household rule and returns a verdict per rule with confidence, not a paragraph.
blueprints.not_jev: OCR of a curved foil packet in supermarket lighting is the actual hard problem.

phases.name: Read the label
phases.detail: Phone camera to OCR. Curved, glossy, low light. Budget most of your effort here.

phases.name: Parse
phases.detail: Ingredient string to a structured list. Additive codes, allergen aliases, sugar synonyms.

phases.name: Score
phases.detail: One typed call carrying every household rule at once. Adding a rule is nearly free.

phases.name: Backfill
phases.detail: Pre-score a catalogue overnight so the common products answer instantly from cache.

phases.name: Ask aloud
phases.detail: Hands full, trolley moving. Voice beats typing in an aisle.

hard_parts: OCR on real packaging is the whole game. The typed scoring is the easy half.
Health claims carry liability. Show the rule that fired and the confidence, never a bare verdict.
blueprints.moat: The pre-scored product cache. It makes the app feel instant and it compounds.

blueprints.name: Constraint-first trip assembler
blueprints.jtbd: When I plan a trip with awkward constraints, I want options that already respect them, so I stop opening twenty tabs to rule things out.
blueprints.who: Families, accessibility needs, dietary needs, pet owners, long-haul workers.
blueprints.why_now: Booking sites filter on price and date. They cannot filter on 'step-free from the platform' or 'quiet room away from the lift'. That is a judgment over prose.
blueprints.jev_role: Reads the messy prose of listings, amenities and reviews and returns a typed verdict per constraint. Also drives the browser agent action choice.
blueprints.not_jev: The browser harness, the search fan-out and the itinerary UI.

phases.name: Gather
phases.detail: Search APIs where they exist. A browser agent for the sites that have none.

phases.name: Judge listings
phases.detail: One typed call per listing carrying every constraint. Noul per hard constraint, Score per soft one.

phases.name: Mine reviews
phases.detail: The truth about step-free access is in review prose, not the amenity list. Score each review.

phases.name: Assemble
phases.detail: Compose the surviving options into whole itineraries and rank them.

phases.name: Stop before buying
phases.detail: Classify the action as irreversible and hand back to the human. Never auto-book.

evidence: A job crawler that matches your profile
hard_parts: Booking sites fight automation. Expect breakage and design for it.
Never let the agent complete a purchase. Classify risk in the same call as the action and stop at irreversible.
Prices move while you deliberate. Re-verify before you show a final number.
blueprints.moat: The constraint vocabulary. Knowing which questions to ask is worth more than the scraping.

blueprints.name: Inbox that triages itself
blueprints.jtbd: When hundreds of messages arrive, I want them already sorted by what they need from me, so I only open the ones that need a person.
blueprints.who: Anyone with a support queue or a drowning inbox.
blueprints.why_now: Two shipped projects handled 63,000 and 1,500 emails. This is the single most proven pattern in the whole corpus.
blueprints.jev_role: Intent, urgency, sentiment, and required action in one typed call per message. Confidence decides auto-file versus human.
blueprints.not_jev: Mail API auth, sync, threading, and the client.

phases.name: Pull
phases.detail: Mail API with incremental sync. Store the raw message beside every verdict.

phases.name: Judge
phases.detail: Intent Choice with a residual 'other', urgency Noul, frustration Score. One call.

phases.name: Route on confidence
phases.detail: High confidence auto-files. Low confidence goes to a review lane. Fit the threshold on labelled mail, do not guess it.

phases.name: Backfill history
phases.detail: Score the archive in a worker pool capped below the rate limit. This is where the 20 calls a second ceiling bites.

phases.name: Search by meaning
phases.detail: Retrieve by intent, not keywords. 'The invoice dispute from March' should just work.

hard_parts: Auto-archiving something important destroys trust permanently. Bias hard toward the review lane.
63,000 messages at one call each is roughly 52 minutes of pure rate-limit floor. Plan the backfill as a batch job.
blueprints.moat: Your labelled corrections. They are what let you raise the auto-file threshold safely.

blueprints.name: Two-sided role and candidate matcher
blueprints.jtbd: When I apply or hire, I want the match judged on substance rather than keyword overlap, so neither side wastes a week.
blueprints.who: Job seekers, small teams without a recruiter.
blueprints.why_now: Keyword ATS matching is famously broken, and per-item judgment is now cheap enough to score every pairing.
blueprints.jev_role: Scores each requirement against each candidate's evidence, and returns the gap list rather than a single number.
blueprints.not_jev: Crawling job boards, parsing CVs, and the application flow.

phases.name: Crawl roles
phases.detail: Job boards mostly resist APIs. A browser agent with a typed action space handles the awkward ones.

phases.name: Structure both sides
phases.detail: Role to requirement list. CV to evidence list. Both typed, both stored.

phases.name: Score the pairing
phases.detail: One call per requirement-evidence pair. Cheap enough to be exhaustive.

phases.name: Return the gap
phases.detail: The useful output is what is missing and whether it is learnable, not a percentage.

evidence: A job crawler that matches your profile
hard_parts: Screening people is regulated and bias-prone. Log every judgment with its evidence and keep a human in the decision.
Never let it auto-reject. Rank and explain only.
blueprints.moat: The requirement taxonomy per role family.

blueprints.name: Clinic intake and triage router
blueprints.jtbd: When a patient describes a problem in their own words, I want it routed to the right clinician with the right urgency, so nothing serious waits behind something trivial.
blueprints.why_now: Only two health projects exist in the corpus, and intake is the lowest-risk, highest-value slice of the category.
blueprints.jev_role: Urgency Score, department Choice, red-flag Nouls. The red flags are the point.
blueprints.not_jev: Scheduling, records, consent, and every compliance surface.

phases.name: Capture
phases.detail: A form that branches on what was already said. Voice for people who struggle to type.

phases.name: Red flags first
phases.detail: A dedicated Noul per emergency symptom, evaluated in the same call. Any hit short-circuits to a human immediately.

phases.name: Route
phases.detail: Department Choice plus urgency Score. Low confidence always means a person looks.

phases.name: Hand off
phases.detail: Structured summary to the clinician, with the patient's own words preserved verbatim.

hard_parts: This is a safety-critical build. It must triage toward caution and never diagnose.
Health data means real regulatory obligations before you write a line of code.
The red-flag questions need clinical review. Do not author them alone.

blueprints.name: Competitive shelf and price watcher
blueprints.jtbd: When I sell a product, I want to know when a competitor changes price, claims or positioning, so I can respond the same day.
blueprints.why_now: Monitoring is a recurring check, which means a deterministic script, not a re-spawned agent. The judgment layer is the only part that needs a model.
blueprints.jev_role: Decides whether a detected change is materially meaningful, so you are alerted on repositioning and not on a whitespace edit.
blueprints.not_jev: Scheduling, diffing, storage, and alert delivery.

phases.name: Snapshot
phases.detail: Scheduled fetch of competitor pages. Embedded JSON first, browser only where needed.

phases.name: Diff
phases.detail: Plain deterministic diff. No model. Most days nothing changed.

phases.name: Judge materiality
phases.detail: Only diffs get a typed call: is this material, which axis, how significant.

phases.name: Watch the imagery
phases.detail: Creative changes matter too. OCR the pack shot and compare claims.

hard_parts: Alert fatigue kills these products. The materiality judgment is the entire value.
Only judge what actually changed, or you will burn the rate limit on unchanged pages.
blueprints.moat: The longitudinal history. Nobody can backfill last year's shelf.

blueprints.name: Document pile to structured ledger
blueprints.jtbd: When a pile of invoices, receipts and statements arrives, I want them classified, extracted and filed, so month-end stops being manual.
blueprints.why_now: Four shipped projects cover the pieces. Nobody has assembled them into one back-office product.
blueprints.jev_role: Document type Choice, a routing decision for which extractor to run, and a confidence gate on every extracted figure.
blueprints.not_jev: OCR, the extractors, the ledger, and the accounting integration.

phases.name: Ingest
phases.detail: Email, scans, photos. Normalise everything to page images plus text.

phases.name: Route per page
phases.detail: Typed call picks the document type and the extractor. Pages differ inside one PDF.

phases.name: Extract
phases.detail: Type-specific extraction. Deterministic where the layout is fixed.

phases.name: Gate the numbers
phases.detail: Money must never be silently wrong. Below threshold goes to human review.

phases.name: File and find
phases.detail: Ledger rows plus retrieval by meaning for audit questions.

hard_parts: A wrong figure in a ledger is worse than no figure. Gate hard and show the source crop.
Document type varies page by page, so route per page and never per file.
blueprints.moat: Per-vendor layout memory. It compounds every month.

blueprints.name: A review gate that reads the diff
blueprints.jtbd: When an agent or a teammate opens a pull request, I want the mechanical objections raised before a human looks, so review time goes on design rather than on catching the obvious.
blueprints.who: Anyone merging code an agent wrote.
blueprints.why_now: Twenty-six shipped projects are pipeline gates and they all found the same thing: adding a check is nearly free because every check rides in one call.
blueprints.jev_role: Runs N independent checks over one diff in a single call and returns a typed verdict per check with confidence.
blueprints.not_jev: Git plumbing, the CI hook, and posting the comment.

phases.name: Get the diff
phases.detail: Per file, with enough surrounding context to judge. Skip lockfiles and generated output.

phases.name: Ask everything at once
phases.detail: One call carrying every rule as its own Noul or Score. Ten rules cost about what one costs.

phases.name: Gate on confidence
phases.detail: Block only on high-confidence failures. Everything else is a comment, not a veto.

phases.name: Track the false positives
phases.detail: A gate nobody trusts gets disabled. Log every override and retire rules that keep being wrong.

evidence: Fourteen checks for every pull request
hard_parts: A noisy gate gets switched off within a week. Precision matters more than coverage.
Rules written as prose drift. Keep them versioned beside the code they judge.
blueprints.moat: The override log. It is the only honest measure of whether a rule earns its place.

blueprints.name: NPCs that decide instead of patrol
blueprints.jtbd: When a player meets a non-player character, I want it to choose plausibly against the current state, so encounters stop being a memorised patrol route.
blueprints.why_now: Eighty-six control-loop projects exist and the frame budget is the whole constraint. A typed decision fits inside it; a generated sentence does not.
blueprints.jev_role: Picks the next action from the moves that are legal right now, and returns the distribution so the character can be plausible instead of optimal.
blueprints.not_jev: The game loop, pathfinding, animation and state serialisation.

phases.name: Serialise the state
phases.detail: Compact text the model can read: positions, health, what the character can see. Keep it small.

phases.name: Offer only legal moves
phases.detail: The code owns the menu. Never offer an action the engine cannot execute.

phases.name: Decide off the frame
phases.detail: Run the call asynchronously and keep acting on the last decision until the next lands.

phases.name: Sample, do not maximise
phases.detail: Use the returned probabilities. Always taking the argmax makes a character that reads as a robot.

evidence: Five hundred agents in a 3D environment
hard_parts: A network call inside a frame budget will stall. Decide asynchronously or accept dropped frames.
Perfect play is not fun. The distribution is the feature, not a defect to round away.
blueprints.moat: None worth defending. Build it because it is the fastest way to learn the control loop.

blueprints.name: A feed you actually wrote the rules for
blueprints.jtbd: When I open a feed, I want my own rules applied rather than the platform's, so I see what I came for.
blueprints.why_now: The most-repeated pattern in the corpus, with a dozen shipped variants. It is also the easiest credible thing to ship in a weekend.
blueprints.jev_role: Scores each post against rules the user wrote in plain language, in the gap before they scroll past.
blueprints.not_jev: The extension, DOM observation, and the settings UI.

phases.name: Observe
phases.detail: MutationObserver on the feed container. Extract text per post as it appears.

phases.name: Batch the visible
phases.detail: Judge the posts near the viewport, not the whole feed. Debounce scrolling.

phases.name: Act gently
phases.detail: Collapse and tag rather than delete. Always show what was hidden and why.

phases.name: Cache verdicts
phases.detail: The same post reappears constantly. Cache by post id or you will pay repeatedly.

evidence: Write your own X feed algorithm
hard_parts: Platform DOM changes without warning. Selector drift is your main maintenance cost.
Judge only what is near the viewport, or one scroll burns hundreds of calls.
Hiding the wrong post is invisible to the user. Make hidden items recoverable.
blueprints.moat: None. Ship it for the portfolio and the learning, not the defensibility.
